keyword.term: average settlement for car accident back and neck injury

irc.what: Auto Injury Insurance Claims: A Study of Increasing Claim Severity
irc.inflation_multiple: more than double the rate of medical care inflation

leverage.quote: BI claimants received $2.00 in total settlement for every dollar of medical bills paid, not accounting for any legal fees.

net.quote: After accounting for medical costs and legal fees (estimated at one-third of settlement), BI claimants with attorneys received $1.40 in claim payment for every dollar of medical expense, compared with $1.80 for claimants without attorneys.

irc.funding: The IRC is a nonprofit research body supported by property and casualty insurers, and affiliated with The Institutes. It says it does not lobby.

sprains.what: a study of bodily injury claims in California, Illinois, Texas and Washington, claims closed in 2002
sprains.quote: In each of the four states, neck or back sprains were the most serious injury for at least seven in ten BI claimants and at least three-quarters suffered no disability from the accident.
sprains.note: Read in the trade press report of the study, not in the IRC's own document, which is not published free.

whiplash_cost.what: Final rule on head restraints, FMVSS No. 202a, 69 Fed. Reg. 74848
whiplash_cost.quote: For rear impact crashes, the average cost of whiplash injuries in 2002 dollars is $9,994 (which includes $6,843 in economic costs and $3,151 in quality of life impacts, but not property damage)

recovery.who: Carroll and colleagues for the Bone and Joint Decade 2000-2010 Task Force on Neck Pain
recovery.quote: The evidence suggests that approximately 50% of those with WAD will report neck pain symptoms 1 year after their injuries.

states.change: Raised from 15/30 for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025, and set to rise again in 2035.

threshold.rule: a permanent injury, significant and permanent scarring or loss of an important bodily function, or death

states.note: Florida requires PIP and property damage cover. Bodily injury liability is not compulsory for most drivers; the 10/20 figures in § 324.021(7) are proof of financial responsibility.

threshold.rule: more than $2,000 in reasonable medical expenses, or a death, a fracture, a lost body member, permanent and serious disfigurement, or loss of sight or hearing

threshold.rule: a serious injury, for a driver who chose limited tort: death, serious impairment of a body function or permanent serious disfigurement

reading.title: NYC Car Accident: Average Settlement for Neck & Back Injuries
reading.why: The same question asked for New York City, where the serious injury threshold decides whether pain and suffering is on the table at all. Its account of the $50,000 no-fault benefit, the 90/180 rule and the three-year deadline matches the statutes. Its value ranges are the firm's own estimates, labelled as such.

reading.title: What is the average settlement for whiplash?
reading.why: Whiplash in Texas, with the state's comparative fault rule worked through an example: a driver more than half to blame recovers nothing, which matches Texas law. The range it gives is the firm's own ballpark.

reading.title: Was Your Back Injured in a Car Accident?
reading.why: The back injuries that move a claim out of the soft tissue band, herniated discs, fractured vertebrae and lumbar damage that stops physical work, explained by an Oregon trial firm.
